name: Building and Deploying AI in Banking and Lending
description: Follow one composite $46 billion bank through a year-long AI program with public promises and OCC examinations on the calendar. Build and test the systems bank AI teams own, from an ML credit model to a servicing assistant, prove what they are worth in savings the CFO can book, and make the strategic trade-offs in six Decision Labs and a capstone simulation.

image.caption: Wirewalk Institute of AI badge: Building and Deploying AI in Banking and Lending

criteria.narrative:
To earn this certificate a learner must: complete all 18 lessons in 6 modules, play each of the course's 7 Decision Labs to an ending (the lab score does not count); and pass the final exam: 20 questions, 40 minutes, pass mark 80%, at most 3 attempts, with a 24-hour wait after a failed attempt.

The exam is taken online and is not proctored. The holder's identity is not verified; the name is the one on their account. This is a certificate of completion and assessment issued by Wirewalk Institute of AI. It is not an accreditation, academic credit, license, or a certification from any vendor. Details: https://institute.wirewalk.com/certification/#limits

alignment.targetName: Evaluate a challenger credit model against the champion at the business's operating point on out-of-time data, and derive per-applicant adverse-action reasons that meet the Regulation B specificity requirement and stay stable under small input changes
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Analyze a credit model for outcome disparities and proxy features, compare less discriminatory alternatives on approvals and disparity, and recommend one in a committee memo that names the federal, state and private-law exposures that remain after the July 21, 2026 Reg B amendments
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Classify each component of a bank AI system as an SR 26-2 model, a deterministic process or a generative or agentic tool outside SR 26-2, tier it by use and materiality, and specify proportionate controls, including an internal standard for out-of-scope tools
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Validate a vendor ML score on the bank's own data, with effective-challenge questions, outcomes by period and segment, and drift detection, and write approval conditions with monitoring triggers, owners and actions
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Set and defend an operating threshold for an AML, fraud or onboarding decision on out-of-time data within a staff-capacity and customer-friction budget, so that recall of the cases that matter holds and the SAR and Regulation E clocks are met
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Test a generative AI tool in lending operations or customer conversations against a gold set with pass thresholds set before testing, covering numbers tied to source, rights-triggering intents and contact and consent rules enforced outside the model, and decide pass, conditional pass or fail
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Create a release decision package for one bank AI use case that combines scope classification, evidence, consumer-law clocks, third-party terms, fairness and customer-harm review, monitoring and a tested rollback, with a recommendation a model risk committee can act on and a one-page board summary
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes

alignment.targetName: Evaluate the business case for a bank AI deployment by separating booked savings from capacity freed and customer losses avoided, netting run and review costs, and choosing build, buy or extend on total cost, traceability, data boundary and change control
alignment.targetFramework: Wirewalk Institute of AI course outcomes
